target_customer: Consumers, restaurants, merchants and couriers in Erbil and other Iraqi cities
problem: Iraq lacked organized on-demand delivery and digital payments in a cash-based, largely unbanked market.
business_model: Marketplace take rate on delivery orders plus payments, taxi and B2B supply chain services

founders.name: Yadgar Merani
previous_startups: Fastwares (software and apps company started with Rekar Botany)
founders.background_notes: YC page: Kurdish Iraqi born in London who moved to Iraq at age 3. Company story page says he and a friend started in a coffee shop in Erbil as Fastwares.

founders.name: Rekar Botany
founders.background_notes: YC page: computer engineer specializing in Node.js and React Native.

technical_complexity.rationale: Standard delivery marketplace apps; the difficulty was operations, address data and payments in an immature market.

defensibility.rationale: Local density of merchants and couriers and a first-mover position in Kurdistan helped, but delivery apps are copyable by regional players.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Talabat announced Erbil entry in October 2020, after the batch, and ride apps Careem and Baly later added delivery. Lezzoo acquired the local rival Erbil Delivery and the B2B marketplace Saydo (December 2022) rather than being acquired.

market_need_then: Iraq was largely cash-based with few delivery options; Wamda (July 2020) describes Lezzoo moving a mostly unbanked population to digital payments through Lezzoo Pay.

branding.name_origin: A Wikipedia-derived summary says the name combines the Badini word Lez and the Sorani word Zoo, both meaning quick. Single source, treat as unverified.

identity.voice_and_tone: Upbeat, direct, concise; tagline 'Bringing you time back'

branding.brand_signature: Kurdish-language name meaning quick, and being the first Iraqi startup accepted by Y Combinator

rebrands.why: The Eats suffix was dropped as the company expanded beyond food; company story page

brand_strength.rationale: Strong local identity and regional press as Iraq's first YC startup and super app, but no sourced evidence of mascot, merch or fan community.

pivots.to: Essentials, payments and a broader super app, then B2B supply chain
pivots.why: Company story page says it pivoted during COVID-19 to essentials and expanded into B2B

outcome_analysis: Lezzoo is active with about 190 staff. It started in Erbil in 2018 with 12 restaurants, joined YC in 2019, closed a seven figure seed in July 2020 and acquired Erbil Delivery and Saydo as it widened into payments and B2B. Total disclosed funding is small at about 1.1 million dollars, so growth appears capital efficient, though later rounds are not public.
notes: The $150K pre-seed amount comes from a Wamda 2022 summary; Wamda 2020 confirms YC pre-seed without an amount. Wamda 2022 gives about $1.1M total raised; Caplight says $1.15M; CB Insights shows only $150K and was ignored. Competitor list left empty: Talabat entry was announced in Oct 2020 and Careem, Toters and Baly delivery dates were not found with dated sources; Erbil Delivery launched in 2018 per iraqtech.io but its article date was not confirmed. Rekar Botany is called co-founder on the YC page and the company story page. No layoffs or shutdown found.
